dedupe_keys.name: mobiliti parallel discrete event regional road traffic simulator lbnl

description: Mobiliti is a software platform that emulates the dynamics of a regional road transportation network using parallel discrete-event simulation built on open-source software. Its record gives the example of a simulation of the whole San Francisco Bay Area, with a network model of about one million links and a population making about 19 million trips, run in about five minutes. The stated intent is a digital twin capability that lets cities evaluate the consequences of infrastructure or policy changes on road network dynamics. It was developed by Jane Macfarlane, Max Bremer and Cy Chan at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and UC Berkeley with US Department of Energy sponsorship, and version 1.0 was registered on DOE CODE on 26 September 2023. The model is generic but was demonstrated at regional scale. It is closed source: questions about obtaining it go to the LBNL licensing office, so access and cost are on request. Caveats: the code and its documentation are not public, and outputs depend on the demand and network inputs supplied. Mobiliti supports large-scale network flow simulation, resilience studies of road closures and digital twins of regional traffic. It complements the BEAM and MATSim agent-based models catalogued here.
